translations.text: Here the Gospel tells how Christ went over the waters of the sea, and about the apostle Peter. This gospel
that was just now read here tells about our Lord Christ, how he went over the waters of the sea,

and about the apostle Peter, who walked in fear, wavering, and sank when he did not believe, and came up again when he believed. It urges us to understand this sea as the present world, and the apostle Peter, in turn,
and came up again. It urges us to understand that this present world is the sea, and that the apostle Peter, in turn,
stands as a sign of the one Christian church. Peter himself, the first in the order of the apostles, the most ready in his love for Christ,
often answers alone for all. When our Lord Jesus Christ asked whom people thought he was,
the disciples answered with the various opinions people held. Again our Lord asked and said:
"But whom do you think that I am?" Peter answered: "You are Christ, the Son of the living God." One gave the answer for many: unity in many. Then
the Lord said to him: "Blessed are you, for flesh did not reveal this to you, but the Father who is in heaven." After that he said: "And I say
to you." It is as if he said: "Because you said, 'You are Christ, the Son of the living God,' I say to you: You are Peter." Before, he was in fact Simon. This, that
he became Peter, was given to him so that he would signify [?] the rock [?], the Christian people. For therefore [?] from the rock, the rock [?], just
as Christian comes from Christ, and upon the rock itself, the rock [?]: "You are Christ [the Son of the] living [God]." [?] church. That is: upon [this rock] I will build my [church] [?]
you, not me [upon you] [?]. Some people said: "I [am] of Apollos," ["I] of Peter." And others [would not be built] upon Peter [?], but [said they were] Christ's [?] apostle [?], and Christ['s] [?]
[This is] our likeness: sometimes he is bold, sometimes he wavers, sometimes he trusts in this immortality,
sometimes he fears that he will die. That is why [?] so, because the church of Christ has the weak, and also has the strong.
It cannot be without the strong, nor without the weak. This is why the apostle Paul also said: "We who are strong ought also to bear the burdens of the weak."
When Peter said, "You are the Son of the living God," he signified the strong. And when
he was afraid and wavered and did not want Christ to suffer martyrdom, fearing death and not recognizing life, he signified the weak
in the church. In this one apostle, that is Peter, the first and foremost in the order of the apostles, in whom
the Christian church was signified, both kinds had to be signified, that is, the strong and the weak,
because without both there is no church. And this is also where what was just read comes from: "Lord, if it is you, command me to come to you
on the waters." "If it is you, command me": I certainly cannot do this by myself, only in you. He recognized what came from himself
and what came from Christ. By Christ's will he trusted that he could do what no human being's weak flesh could do. "So if it is you,
command," because when you command, it will happen; what I cannot do by daring, you, Lord, can do by commanding. And the Lord said:
Peter came without any doubt at the word of the one commanding, [?] of the one sustaining, at the presence of the Power; without any hesitation he leapt into the water and began to walk.
He was able to do that, not at all from himself, but from the Lord, the saving Christ. For you were once darkness, but now
light in the Lord. What no one can do in Paul, no one in Peter, no one in another, nor in any one of the apostles, that
one can truly do in the Lord. Therefore Paul, wisely setting himself aside, commended Christ well and said: Was Paul for
you crucified on the cross, or were you baptized in his name? Therefore not in me, but with me; not
under me, but under the Lord. Therefore Peter went over the waters at God's command. He knew that he could not have such power
from himself. In firm faith he was able to do what human weakness could not. These are the firm ones of the Church.
Hear, understand, perceive, act. For it is not to be done in earnest with the firm that they become weak;
rather, it is to be done with the weak that they become firm. But a foolish presumption of firmness hinders many from
firmness. No one becomes firm by God except one who feels himself weak of himself. Voluntary rain
God sets apart for his inheritance. Why do you run ahead, you who know what I am going to say? Let speed moderate itself so that slowness may follow.
This I said and this I say: hear, understand, act. No one becomes firm by God except one who of
himself feels himself weak. Rain, voluntary rain, as the Psalmist says: voluntary, not because of our merits,
